thread.title: Netflix Stock Bolstered By European Subscriber Gains |

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Netflix Stock Bolstered By European Subscriber Gains |
text:
Internet television network Netflix ( NFLX ) is making big subscriber gains in Europe while it holds its lead in the U.S., a new survey indicates.
X RBC Capital Markets on Friday reported the results from its latest consumer survey, which backs its positive thesis on Netflix stock. RBC analyst Mark Mahaney reiterated his outperform rating on Netflix stock with a price target of 450.
Netflix stock fell 6.3% to 265.14 during an overall down session on the stock market today .
Since hitting an all-time high of 423.21 on June 21, Netflix has fallen 37.4% through Friday's close. Shares have tumbled on concerns about competition coming in 2019 from Walt Disney ( DIS ), AT&T 's ( T ) WarnerMedia and Apple ( AAPL ).

Please contact customer service CLOSE RBC surveyed 1,650 consumers in the U.S. and over 2,000 in France and 2,000 in Germany to gauge usage and satisfaction with Netflix. It found record high usage levels in all three countries.
In France, 40% of respondents are using Netflix, up from 24% in a November 2017 survey. In Germany, 41% of respondents are using Netflix, up from 29% a year earlier, RBC said.
Also, 91% of French subscribers and 90% of German subscribers are "extremely" or "very satisfied" with Netflix. That's consistent with strong results over the last year, Mahaney said in a report.
Netflix Churn A Concern In U.S. Market In the U.S., 59% of respondents watch Netflix. That compares with 57% in August and 56% in November 2017, RBC said.
However, rivals also are quickly rising, Mahaney said. Some 48% of respondents watch Amazon ( AMZN ) streaming video and 38% watch Hulu.
The U.S. survey found that 69% of Netflix subscribers are "extremely" or "very satisfied" with the service. That's consistent with the last six quarters, Mahaney said.
On a negative note, expectations for churn rose to the highest level in the last 27 quarterly surveys, RBC said. The latest survey found that 9.4% of U.S. subscribers say they are "very" or "extremely likely" to cancel Netflix.
